body.heading: The push-through myth
paragraphs: We admire the person who pushes through, and rest can look suspiciously like giving up. But watch anything that lasts — athletes, musicians, farmers, parents — and you will find rest built into the rhythm, not stolen from it. Muscles repair between sessions. Fields recover between plantings. People are not exceptions.
When you are coming back from a hard stretch, rest is not a pause in the recovery. On many days, rest is the recovery.

body.heading: Rest that actually restores
paragraphs: Not all stopping is rest. Lying on the sofa scrolling through alarming news is stopping; it rarely restores. Rest tends to involve some mix of sleep, low-demand pleasure, gentle movement, daylight and the company of people around whom you can be unguarded.

Notice what genuinely refills you and write it down for the days when you cannot think. A personal rest menu — bath, walk, music, early night, an hour with a undemanding book — is a tool you build in good times for use in hard ones.

body.heading: Rest before you are empty
paragraphs: The deeper skill is resting before collapse: the evening off taken while you could still have pushed, the weekend kept clear ahead of the busy month. Planned rest feels indulgent right up until you compare it with the alternative.

If exhaustion persists despite real rest — weeks of it, affecting work, mood or health — treat that as information worth sharing with a doctor or another professional. Bodies sometimes ask for help in this language, and they deserve to be listened to.

takeaway: Build rest into the rhythm, on the good days, so the hard days have something to draw on.
